quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:

options.text: Excessive stops.
Sudden stops.
Sudden turns.
Driving too fast.

questions.explanation: At high speeds, your tires cannot clear water from the road. Your tires lose grip and your car slides on water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
0.02 percent.
0.1 percent.

questions.explanation: For drivers age 21 or older, the legal limit is a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: You are in the right lane of a multilane highway and want to move to the left lane. You should:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. Always signal when you change lanes.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, the safest way is to:

options.text: Change your speed frequently to stay alert.
Drive faster than other vehicles.
Drive slower than other vehicles.
Drive at the same speed as other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than surrounding vehicles. Drive with traffic flow, within the speed limit.

questions.question: To change lanes, you should:

options.text: Check mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, then change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no one is entering the same lane. Then change lanes safely.

questions.question: The posted speed limit shows:

options.text: A recommended speed only.
The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe speed in ideal road and weather conditions.
The maximum safe speed in all conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed in ideal road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the maximum legal speed. Drive slower when conditions are bad, such as rain, fog, or wet roads.

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, use ____ to show you are turning.

options.text: Your horn.
Your headlights.
Hand signals.
Your emergency flashers.

questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to tell other drivers which direction you are turning.

questions.question: You are entering a busy freeway. What should you do to merge safely?

options.text: Use your mirrors and check your blind spots.
Speed up to match the freeway traffic on the entrance ramp.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to reach freeway speed. Yield to cars already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots before you merge.

questions.question: If your wheels go onto the shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.
Stop your car at the road's edge.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed without hard braking. Carefully steer back onto the road. Watch for nearby traffic.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:

options.text: Speed limit sign.
Stop sign.
Hospital sign.
Railroad warning sign.

questions.explanation: All octagonal signs are stop signs. Come to a complete stop at every red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: Many crashes happen because:

options.text: Drivers go too fast for current conditions.
Drivers check mirrors and blind spots often.
Drivers give the right-of-way to others.
Drivers keep a four-second distance behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers go too fast for current conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen when drivers go too fast for conditions. Always drive at legal speeds and slow down when conditions are bad.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep your normal speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Let pedestrians cross first.
Drive faster than usual.

questions.explanation: You can turn right or left at a green light if no sign blocks it. When turning, you must let other cars and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you must always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing the tracks.
Pay attention and follow all traffic signals.
Share the road with walkers and cyclists.
All of these.

questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks and obey all signs and signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicycles.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light means:

options.text: The same thing as a stop sign.
The traffic light is broken.
You do not have to stop completely.
Driving is very dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: You can drink alcohol in a car on a public road:

options.text: If you are not driving.
If you sit in the back seat.
If you ride in the back of a pickup truck.
Never.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have open alcohol in a car on any public road. You also cannot have open alcohol in the driver or passenger area of any car on a public road.

questions.question: Which one must you follow over the others?

options.text: A steady red light
A police officer
A stop sign
A flashing red light

questions.explanation: Traffic officers' directions are more important than signs, lights, or road markings. Traffic officers include police, fire police, road work flag people, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Entering or leaving a parking space.
Entering traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal every time you move left or right. Signal when entering traffic from a parking space, changing lanes, or passing another car.

questions.question: When entering a road from a private driveway, you should:

options.text: Honk to warn other cars you are coming.
Park partly on the road to alert drivers.
Drive out fast to blend with traffic.
Let pedestrians and road traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians and road traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When entering a road from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and traffic on the road pass first.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Bridge getting narrower ahead.
Lane is ending or road is getting narrower ahead.
Industrial area.
Freeway entrance ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane is ending or road is getting narrower ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped with black symbols on yellow. They tell drivers about hazards coming. This sign warns that the right lane is ending or the road is narrowing.

questions.question: When passing on a two-lane road with traffic going both ways, you should:

options.text: Return to your lane when you have enough space between you and the passed car.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Go back to the right lane right away.
Drive in any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to your lane when you have enough space between you and the passed car.
questions.explanation: When passing on a two-lane road, return to the right lane when there is enough space between you and the car you passed.
